changes.title: Hive: connect an Organization and share supported event, customer and purchase updates
changes.text: The Integrations page adds Connect, Reconnect and Disconnect for Hive, plus a clear description of the data shared. Backend jobs send supported event changes, customer contact and saved marketing preferences, and completed ticket purchases. A purchase does not subscribe a customer to marketing.
changes.impact: Organizations using the Hive pilot can keep supported Showpass data current without a manual send for every edit.
changes.limits: Requires integration-management permission, enable_hive_integration and configured Hive credentials. Initial event population remains operator-run. Purchase export supports completed, unadjusted ordinary ticket sales; mixed unsupported items and package child lines are excluded. Disconnect stops future sends but does not remove data already accepted by Hive. Hive processing and campaign revenue attribution were not tested.

changes.title: Developer API keys: limit integration access and inspect request history
changes.text: Adds backend APIs to issue, list and revoke Organization-specific developer keys. A key is tied to an active employee and selected operations. The secret is returned once; expiry, revocation, current employee permissions, request limits and separate password-reading permission are enforced. Authorized employees can read retained request diagnostics.
changes.impact: Integrations can receive narrower access than a full employee login, and support can investigate requests without exposing the key secret.
changes.limits: This diff establishes backend capabilities, not a newly verified Dashboard management screen. Requires the new key schema, configured authentication and request-log storage in ClickHouse. Access to other Organizations and unsupported routes is rejected; live retention/configuration were not checked.

changes.title: Webhook diagnostics hide credentials and unsafe receiver echoes
changes.text: Organizer-visible webhook diagnostics remove credential fields from nested data, redact sensitive headers, and strip credentials, query strings and fragments from destination URLs. Receiver response bodies are hidden when they could echo private request values.
changes.impact: Employees troubleshooting an integration have less opportunity to expose signing secrets or authentication data.
changes.limits: This is a change to diagnostic visibility. It does not prove every historical log, external receiver or monitoring destination has been sanitized.

changes.title: Workflow approvers can preview ticket prices and fees
changes.text: The event preview opened from a publication-approval workflow adds Pricing & fees. It separates what the Customer pays from what the Organizer absorbs, with currency, calculation time and ticket-level fee details. The backend resolves the event through the authorized review and does not create an order.
changes.impact: Approvers can review the cost of a ticket without asking another team to calculate it or entering checkout.
changes.limits: Examples use the latest saved pricing for one online ticket paid by card. They are not frozen submitted prices, a whole-basket quote or a payout calculation. Configured-fee events are supported; payment-plan ticket types are marked unsupported.

changes.title: Workflow submissions retain the right review state, links and PDF answers
changes.text: Submission, withdrawal, approval and denial can reject an action based on an outdated review round. Notification jobs retain the intended round, suppress stale or duplicate sends, and build the review link with the correct workflow identifier. PDF choice fields show the selected labels instead of internal option values.
changes.impact: Reviewers are less likely to open the wrong submission or act on an old state, and submitted answers are easier to read.
changes.limits: Requires the paired backend and frontend workflow changes. Duplicate-email and concurrent-action behavior were not executed during this digest run; historical Jira comments are separate evidence.

changes.title: Custom messages explain an unannounced event date or time
changes.text: Adds separate messages for an unknown date-and-time and an unknown time on a known date. Ticket Type overrides take priority over Event overrides, then Organization defaults. Customer-facing schedule data carries the resolved message into supported pages, orders, emails and wallet-update paths.
changes.impact: An Organizer can explain when scheduling information will be announced instead of showing only a generic TBD label.
changes.limits: Messages are trimmed and limited to 256 characters; a blank override falls back to the next setting. Requires the Venue/Event/Ticket Type migrations and compatible clients/workers. Live wallet delivery and every client were not tested. Jira still says On Deck despite code on develop.

changes.title: Shared ticket Inventory protects reserved quantities and overall Capacity
changes.text: Adds backend and Admin support for several Ticket Types to share one Event Capacity. Each Ticket Type can have a protected quantity and an optional maximum. Basket and waitlist admission checks account for the shared pool; resale and held-allocation changes avoid counting or returning the same places twice.
changes.impact: A configured Event can share unsold places across ticket categories while protecting reserved allocations.
changes.limits: Pools belong to one concrete Event occurrence and Organization; a recurring parent is not a valid owner. Management requires Manage Events permission. No new Dashboard pool editor was established in the frontend diff. Concurrent purchases, resale completion/cancellation and physical admission were not executed.

changes.title: The public guest-list form moves to the newer interface
changes.text: Adds a public guest-list page with widget-specific fields, event selection, birthday handling, manual entry and Facebook import. The form prevents a second submission while a request is pending, shows field errors and confirms a saved request. The server checks the widget, Organization, available Event and guest-count limits before saving a pending reservation. Follow-up layout changes separate Facebook import from manual entry and add submit-button spacing.
changes.impact: Visitors have a clearer signup flow, while a rejected or unsaved request is not counted as a successful registration.
changes.limits: Existing embedded links switch only when enable_public_guestlist_nextjs_embed is active for the Venue; otherwise they keep the legacy form. A saved guest-list request is pending, not confirmed admission. Required custom questions are enforced by the client; server validation checks supplied answer values. This run did not submit a guest-list request.

changes.title: Organizer profiles keep Queue-it protection during page navigation
changes.text: The public Organization data exposes its configured Queue-it setting, and the newer Organizer profile loads the existing queue integration when eligible. Client-side route changes recheck the protected destination after Queue-it configuration is ready.
changes.impact: Moving between public pages within the app does not rely solely on the queue check from the first full page load.
changes.limits: Applies to configured Queue-it Organizations and supported protected pages. The provider configuration must be available; readiness errors are recorded. No live queue challenge or admission test was run.

changes.title: Bandsintown activation records cost acceptance and checks fee setup
changes.text: The legacy Integrations page adds an Organizer enablement flow. The server verifies or provisions the applicable Bandsintown fee configuration before enabling the Venue. Disablement is restricted to an authorized Admin.
changes.impact: An Organization can accept the integration cost explicitly rather than enabling it with an incomplete or conflicting fee configuration.
changes.limits: This is opt-in/disablement work, not proof that all event publishing or reporting phases of the Bandsintown integration are complete. The fee selector covers eligible ticket sales on Web, Widget and Mobile, with specified payment types. Conflicting fee cards block activation; no setting was changed here.

changes.title: Seasonal membership revenue stays with eligible benefits and preserves rounding
changes.text: New seasonal allocation work uses the applicable group-level benefits rather than adding membership-level benefits into the same split. Revenue and fee distribution respect each eligible benefit’s allocation and retain cent-level totals. Existing allocation records retain their legacy eligibility.
changes.impact: Finance reporting is less likely to split a season-pass purchase into an unintended benefit or distribute more than its allocated share.
changes.limits: This concerns seasonal membership revenue allocation, not the member’s admission rights. Existing records are not described as a blanket historical repair. Financial reconciliation and new-season processing were not executed.

changes.title: Voucher returns restore combined usage across order lines
changes.text: When several returned order lines used the same voucher, the refunder combines their usage and restores the limit on a freshly locked voucher record. It also clears the cached voucher balance after the change is committed.
changes.impact: A returned FlexPass or voucher purchase is less likely to leave part of the Customer’s permitted uses unavailable for a replacement purchase.
changes.limits: Requires enable_voucher_refund_limit_fix. The previous path remains when the switch is off. No live voucher balance or refund was changed, and switch state is unknown.

changes.title: Package exchange calculations use credit at the matching order-line scope
changes.text: Refund/exchange calculations use the credit amount recorded at the same reporting scope as the order line’s totals. Package parents include child credit without taking an unrelated child-only amount a second time.
changes.impact: The amount available during a package exchange is less likely to be understated or counted at the wrong level.
changes.limits: This source change does not establish a general refund entitlement or a verified final payment amount. No Exchange, Refund or credit record was created.

changes.title: Resale waitlists continue to later buyers when the first request cannot fit
changes.text: The scheduler considers subscribers in queue order but continues when a buyer has no compatible resale supply or complete quantity match. That buyer stays pending while a later compatible buyer can be considered.
changes.impact: A request that cannot currently be filled no longer stops all later compatible resale requests.
changes.limits: Complete resale submissions are still matched together; this is not permission to split every listing or skip an eligible buyer. Background scheduling and customer emails were not run.

changes.title: Upgraded tickets can still offer their configured upsells
changes.text: An upgraded ticket is no longer excluded solely by its replacement marker when finding its currently configured upsell paths.
changes.impact: Customers using an upgraded ticket can be offered eligible extras rather than losing the upsell path because an upgrade occurred.
changes.limits: Existing basket, package, seating and sale validation still apply. No upgrade or additional purchase was executed.

changes.title: Admin schedule editing uses the Event or Venue’s local time
changes.text: Shared Admin fields resolve entered local dates and times using the relevant timezone, retain the intended local schedule and report invalid or conflicting changes. Event and membership schedule forms use the shared handling, including Admin history/reconciliation paths.
changes.impact: An Admin editing a season or Event schedule has clearer local-time controls and fewer opportunities for the stored time to disagree with the entered schedule.
changes.limits: Timezone policy and rollout configuration still govern resolution. Repeated or nonexistent daylight-saving times require the supported handling; this run did not save an Admin form or test a clock-change boundary.

changes.title: Box Office postal answers can populate the normal Customer postal field
changes.text: For eligible staff Box Office sales, a valid purchaser postal answer can fill a missing invoice postal address and update the linked Customer address. The code recognizes the built-in purchaser postal value or one unambiguous valid postal/ZIP text answer. Will Call export can fall back to the invoice’s postal code when the guest value is blank.
changes.impact: Collected postal information can appear in the normal Customer address and standard reporting rather than remaining only a custom answer.
changes.limits: This adds backend mapping, not a new standalone postal input. Existing invoice postal values are preserved. Eligible saved purchaser data is used; individual Attendee answers are not treated as the buyer’s address. Jira is still On Deck; no sale or Customer was changed.

changes.title: Box Office delivery details use the Event timezone
changes.text: Delivery-date formatting prefers the Event timezone supplied on the basket line and falls back to the existing timezone only when it is absent.
changes.impact: An Event held in a different timezone from the Organization is less likely to show conflicting times between the cart and delivery details.
changes.limits: This is a display correction. It does not reschedule the Event, and no checkout was executed.

changes.title: Embedded Events List improves contrast, keyboard focus and retry
changes.text: The legacy embedded Events List updates its accessible presentation and Load more behavior. A keyboard user retains a focus target while loading; completion restores useful focus, and a failed page request can be retried instead of permanently ending pagination.
changes.impact: Visitors using keyboard navigation or needing clearer contrast have a more usable embedded list.
changes.limits: Applies to the legacy embedded Events List, not every public listing. Contrast, screen-reader announcements and keyboard behavior were source-reviewed but not browser-tested.

changes.title: Photo Ops pages show clearer prices, biographies and mobile information
changes.text: Talent pages shorten desktop biography presentation, omit empty Information content, and show a clearer base-price/currency/fee explanation. Related copy uses Photo Ops and Autographs & More; autograph/selfie bookings omit an unhelpful standalone Time TBD label. Talent filters extend across the page, and mobile names, subtext and day badges use larger defined text sizes.
changes.impact: Customers can reach the available experiences sooner and better understand the price and useful details on smaller screens.
changes.limits: These are changes within the Photo Ops/Talent flow, not evidence that the full Photo Ops product is launched. Ordinary confirmed times and the full unknown-date fallback remain. Browser responsiveness and purchase completion were not tested.

changes.title: Experience quantities use the experience selection flow
changes.text: Public cart and checkout Review show an experience ticket’s current quantity as text rather than exposing the generic quantity dropdown or increment control. Ordinary admission tickets and Product Extras retain their quantity controls. Edit and Remove actions are aligned together in the legacy cart.
changes.impact: Customers are guided back through the experience editor instead of creating a grouped experience booking that it cannot open.
changes.limits: Classification comes from the Ticket Type’s experience_type. Existing quantities above one remain visible; another experience can be added through its selection flow. This is not a general limit of one ticket.

changes.title: Free checkout no longer waits for a payment handler to identify a zero total
changes.text: The payment screen derives free and waitlist presentation from the basket itself, including complimentary hold links. Validation follows the current payment mode rather than briefly relying on a handler that is still being resolved.
changes.impact: Customers moving into Payment with a zero-dollar basket, including a discounted Exchange, should see a steadier free-payment section.
changes.limits: Free, waitlist and regular payment modes remain distinct. No payment, Exchange or zero-total purchase was executed in this run.

changes.title: A standalone ticket does not inherit another package’s included tickets
changes.text: Checkout’s package-detail selection follows the saved parent relationship. A separately purchased ticket is not displayed as a package merely because its Ticket Type also appears inside another package.
changes.impact: Review shows the intended package children and standalone quantity, avoiding an apparent duplicate-ticket count.
changes.limits: Applies to the split-display Review path. The shared Box Office hook retains its default parent selection behavior. No basket was changed.

changes.title: Automatic-discount labels appear only on discounted rows
changes.text: A Review row now requires a matching discount group before displaying a basket-wide automatic-discount label.
changes.impact: Customers are less likely to believe an undiscounted ticket received a promotion.
changes.limits: This changes label selection, not the server’s discount calculation. Jira remains On Deck; pricing was not tested.

changes.title: Membership transfers open for the selected game and list Events by date
changes.text: The My Orders transfer entry can retain the selected Event context and open the matching transfer flow. Transfer items are sorted by their Event start time.
changes.impact: A season-pass holder is less likely to start transferring tickets for the wrong game or work through an unsorted list.
changes.limits: Existing account access and transfer eligibility checks still apply. No ticket ownership was transferred.

changes.title: Ticket and product financial controls follow the server’s editing capability
changes.text: Finance and Custom Fees honor explicit enable_price_changes instead of treating every raw price lock as a complete editing ban. Locked and unconfirmed states have clearer explanations, including when to add a new item or reload.
changes.impact: Price-tier-enabled Organizations can reach permitted editing controls, and employees get a useful reason when editing is unavailable.
changes.limits: Existing permissions and backend save rules remain. Jira comments record that some locked service-fee changes can still be discarded by the existing server rule; editable controls do not promise every field will save. Missing/null capability remains read-only. No fee was saved here.

changes.title: Unset sale-start calendars open on the current month
changes.text: Individual and bulk Ticket Type sale-start editors no longer borrow the future Event start date merely to choose the opening calendar month. Saved custom dates remain the selected values.
changes.impact: An employee opening sales tomorrow for an Event months away does not need to navigate back through those months first.
changes.limits: Applies to the newer Ticket Types editors. Opening an unset picker does not itself save a sale date. Existing date bounds and timezone handling remain.

changes.title: An existing recurring Event can be reduced to one occurrence
changes.text: Basic Info allows a one-row schedule payload for an Event that is already recurring, so the backend can perform its supported conversion to a single Event.
changes.impact: An Organizer is no longer blocked by the frontend’s two-date minimum when removing the other occurrences.
changes.limits: Creating a recurring Event from a single Event still requires at least two dates. Existing backend conversion and purchase safeguards remain; no Event was converted.

changes.title: Ticket Types waits for its saved draft before showing an empty state
changes.text: The page checks that the local Ticket Type draft belongs to the loaded Event before treating it as ready for the empty-ticket presentation.
changes.impact: An Event with Ticket Types is less likely to briefly show an empty section while its draft initializes.
changes.limits: This concerns the loading-to-ready display transition; it does not create or remove Ticket Types.

changes.title: Creating a custom fee keeps the selected fee type
changes.text: The New custom rate action calls the draft opener explicitly instead of passing the click event into an argument that can affect the new definition.
changes.impact: Selecting a fee is less likely to open a tax-shaped draft by mistake.
changes.limits: Applies to the custom-fee creation control; no fee or tax record was created.

changes.title: Internal-fee defaults do not depend on dropdown ordering
changes.text: Add Fee selects Fee Tax and GST by their defined identities rather than the first items in a generated list, including reset and fee-type changes.
changes.impact: Adding Bandsintown to the available fee types does not silently change the default fee choice.
changes.limits: This is the internal Add Fee form, separate from the custom-rate opener above. Existing fee permissions and save validation remain.

changes.title: Event cards do not show a comma for a missing city or province
changes.text: The Event-card location subtitle joins only the city and province values that are present.
changes.impact: An Event with incomplete location details has a cleaner card label.
changes.limits: Display only; saved location data is unchanged.

changes.title: Products show image placeholders while loading
changes.text: The migrated Products catalog uses a responsive product-shaped loading card, including the image, category, title, Inventory summary, actions and progress area.
changes.impact: The loading layout better matches the product cards that appear afterward.
changes.limits: A loading-display change; image delivery and product editing were not tested.

changes.title: Organizer Settings labels use sentence case
changes.text: Settings navigation labels such as Business schedule, Shipping & fulfillment and Digital wallets use consistent sentence case.
changes.impact: The Organization settings menu is easier to scan consistently.
changes.limits: Only label capitalization is included from the broader Jira feedback. Date-picker, time-dropdown and schedule-layout requests are not claimed as fixed.

changes.title: Search metadata uses the available admission price with fees
changes.text: Event offer metadata reads the API’s online card price excluding tax instead of the raw base Ticket Type price. Unsupported or ambiguous price forms omit that value instead of guessing.
changes.impact: Search engines receive a price that better matches the supported public all-in presentation.
changes.limits: Pay-what-you-can, automatic-discount and payment-plan cases do not get a guessed offer price. This is metadata, not a change to checkout charges or a verified search-result update.

changes.title: Showpass organization metadata has the updated postal address
changes.text: The shared organization metadata uses the Macleod Trail office address, postal code T2H 2N1 and country code CA.
changes.impact: Pages using this metadata no longer publish the previous Showpass office address to search engines.
changes.limits: Does not edit an Organizer’s Event location or billing address.

changes.title: ISO weekday formats no longer raise an unnecessary warning
changes.text: The shared date formatter recognizes the supported ISO weekday token rather than reporting it as an unrecognized date format before producing the weekday.
changes.impact: Supported Talent/website date formatting produces less misleading application-error noise.
changes.limits: This does not change the timezone policy or intentionally suppress warnings for genuinely unknown formats.

changes.title: Invalid map coordinates produce a validation message
changes.text: Malformed coordinate values are converted into “Enter numeric latitude and longitude separated by a comma.” rather than leaking a conversion exception.
changes.impact: An employee entering invalid coordinates can receive a useful correction instead of an internal failure.
changes.limits: This changes coordinate parsing, not geocoding or the full permitted geographic range.

changes.title: Checkout and public-page analytics share event identity and count observed actions
changes.text: Browser and server tracking retain shared event identifiers. Cart tracking counts accepted quantity increases rather than removals or a repeated total, and purchase tracking retains the purchase attempt’s identity through later basket refreshes. Public views respect visibility, and refund-protection attempts carry clearer lifecycle tracking. Conversion reporting counts observed item views rather than filling missing views from add-to-cart counts.
changes.impact: Marketing and product reports can better distinguish real actions, duplicates and missing tracking instead of hiding gaps behind inferred numbers.
changes.limits: Shared callers include public ticket, membership, product, calendar, widget and Website Builder purchase entry points. Reported steps are session/basket journey units, not unique visitors. External pixel delivery, warehouse completion and live report totals were not verified.

changes.title: Gift-card recipient links follow the configured Showpass site
changes.text: The recipient email builds its home and account-credit links from the configured site URL rather than hard-coding the production domain.
changes.impact: A recipient is directed to the matching site when the email is generated in another configured environment.
changes.limits: Only URL construction was reviewed. No gift card or email was sent.

changes.title: Finance can classify a Venue as Bounce without changing its Google ticket-feed treatment
changes.text: Adds the Bounce client type and treats it like Regular for the Google event-service ticket inventory and price fields.
changes.impact: An internal client classification can be changed without unintentionally changing the expected ticket-feed category.
changes.limits: Jira remains On Deck. No Venue classification or Google feed was changed or published.

changes.title: Backend runtime and requests dependency are updated
changes.text: Backend runtime and CI images move from Python 3.12.10 to 3.12.16; requests moves from 2.32.3 to 2.34.2. Timezone adapters use the existing governed-zone reader contract for supported timezone objects.
changes.impact: Updates the configured runtime/dependency baseline while preserving the intended timezone-reading policy.
changes.limits: Repository image references do not prove a deployed interpreter or vulnerability status. No deployment, dependency installation or full application suite was run.

changes.title: Frontend builds declare cache inputs, outputs and TypeScript profiles
changes.text: Build work separates immutable strict/relaxed TypeScript profiles, declares task inputs and environment dependencies, and excludes Next.js’s internal cache from saved deploy outputs. Documentation updates the corresponding commands.
changes.impact: Cached build results have clearer boundaries, and selecting a TypeScript mode does not require rewriting the tracked base configuration.
changes.limits: This report does not claim a measured build-time improvement or a passing CI run.

changes.title: CI reports possible work reduction and prepares a guarded remote-cache pilot
changes.text: Adds a change-selection report and explicit remote-cache policy/summary tooling for a controlled pilot.
changes.impact: The team can inspect which jobs might be avoidable and assess cache behavior before broadening its use.
changes.limits: The added reporting does not prove that all unaffected jobs are now skipped, that remote caching is enabled, or that CI became faster.

changes.title: Operator tools prepare scoped membership and package recovery
changes.text: Adds separate guarded scripts for a missing Kimberley season-pass membership, reviewed MEGACON package-child corrections, and Fan Expo Will Call digital-ticket settings/confirmation recovery.
changes.impact: An authorized operator has a bounded repair procedure instead of rerunning general checkout or fulfillment for all orders.
changes.limits: Files default to preview/dry-run and have different side effects and approval needs. Script presence does not prove any affected order was repaired, a QR code delivered or an email received. None of these scripts was executed.

changes.title: Operator tools prepare Talent import and reviewed fee/package setup
changes.text: Adds a one-time Fan Expo Talent spreadsheet import and separate reviewed Cowboys fee/Fan Expo package configuration scripts.
changes.impact: Operational setup can follow explicit manifests and dry-run output.
changes.limits: These are operator tools, not automatic product rollout or completed setup. No import, fee change, package change or publish operation was run.

changes.title: Tests isolate external services and retain focused regression checks
changes.text: Backend test helpers isolate AI-provider and Google Maps calls; integration tests narrow broker/webhook assertions. The diff also adds behavior-specific tests, email-link inventory checks, translations and internal runbooks supporting the changes above.
changes.impact: The saved checks and helpers make the intended behavior easier to repeat without unrelated external service failures.
changes.limits: Application tests were inventoried but not executed during this digest. Passing results written in a PR or Jira comment remain historical reports by their authors, not results from this run.

changes.title: Membership scanning reuses the loaded candidate records
changes.text: The membership scan service identifies active access from the member records already loaded with the barcode candidates, rather than issuing an additional filtered lookup.
changes.impact: Reduces avoidable database work in a busy admission path while keeping redemption revalidation in place.
changes.limits: This is a source-level query reduction, not a measured scanner speedup or proof of physical-device behavior. No membership was scanned.

changes.title: The Organizer profile header leaves more room for offerings
changes.text: The profile replaces the large desktop hero with a small image beside the Organizer details. Phones show the image above the name. The header retains the appropriate details while scrolling, and the navigation logo aligns with the page content.
changes.impact: Visitors reach Events and other offerings sooner without losing the Organizer identity and navigation.
changes.limits: Applies to the newer Organizer profile. Existing artwork and actions are retained; narrow-screen wrapping, scrolling and keyboard focus were not browser-tested.

presentation.format: Grouped digest with shared QA regression at the end

groups.title: Checkout, purchases and returns
bullets: Free checkout identifies zero-dollar baskets earlier; Review keeps standalone tickets separate from package children and puts automatic-discount labels on the right rows.
Voucher returns restore combined usage, package Exchange calculations use the matching credit amounts, and upgraded tickets keep eligible upsells.
Box Office improves postal-code saving and Event-timezone display. Experience tickets use their selection flow for quantity changes; gift-card emails use the configured site links.
groups.note: Voucher restoration requires its rollout switch. Existing backend fee and return rules still apply.

groups.title: Ticket Inventory, memberships and admission
bullets: Adds backend/Admin support for Ticket Types sharing an Event Capacity, with protected quantities and optional maximums.
Resale waitlists continue to later compatible buyers when an earlier request cannot fit.
Membership scanning reuses loaded records; My Orders transfers keep the selected game and list Events by date.
groups.note: The feature team owns shared-pool setup and rule testing. Shared QA checks existing sales, holds, transfers and admission still work.

groups.title: Dashboard Event setup and approvals
bullets: Workflow approvers get Pricing & fees examples. Submission handling protects the current review round, email links and readable PDF answers.
Adds configurable unknown-date/time messages and improves Admin local-time editing, sale-start calendars and recurring-to-single Event conversion.
Financial controls follow the server’s editing capability; fee creation keeps the selected type. Loading states, location validation and labels receive smaller corrections.
groups.note: Pricing examples use current saved values, not a frozen approval quote. Existing server restrictions can still prevent some locked fee fields from saving.

groups.title: Public pages, Widgets and Photo Ops
bullets: Adds the newer public guest-list form, preserves configured Queue-it protection during navigation, and makes Organizer profile headers more compact.
Photo Ops pages clarify prices and fees, shorten biographies and improve mobile text. The legacy embedded Events List improves contrast, focus and retry behavior.
Search metadata uses the supported admission price with fees and the updated Showpass address; ISO weekday formatting avoids an unnecessary warning.
groups.note: Existing guest-list embeds stay on the legacy form unless the Venue rollout flag is enabled. These changes do not establish a full Photo Ops launch.

groups.title: Integrations and developer access
bullets: Hive gains connection management and supported Event, Customer-preference and completed ticket-purchase sharing.
Developer keys limit integration access by Organization, employee and permitted operation, with request-history APIs. Webhook diagnostics hide credentials.
Bandsintown opt-in checks fee setup and cost acceptance, with Admin-only disablement.
groups.note: Owning teams validate credentials, scopes, consent, fees and provider acceptance. No integration setting was changed during this review.

groups.title: Financial reporting and analytics
bullets: Seasonal membership revenue follows eligible benefit allocations and preserves rounding.
Checkout tracking shares browser/server identities, counts accepted quantity increases and reports observed views instead of filling tracking gaps with assumptions.
Adds the Bounce client classification while retaining Regular-style Google ticket-feed treatment.
groups.note: Report totals and external analytics delivery remain unverified. Jira status does not establish that any change is deployed.

groups.title: Internal engineering and operator tools
bullets: Backend runtime and dependencies update; frontend build/cache boundaries and CI reporting become more explicit.

checks.title: Complete an ordinary paid sale
checks.start: Public Web and an existing embedded Widget; then Web Box Office.
checks.check: Buy an ordinary ticket on a clean successful path. Confirm one charge, one saved order, the exact issued tickets, correct fees/taxes and Showpass earnings, one Inventory reduction and usable receipt links.
checks.why: Basket, payment, Inventory and analytics code changed.
checks.clients: Public Web, Widget, Web Box Office; supported Electron and mobile/POS staff-sale smoke

checks.title: Keep free and failed payment paths usable
checks.start: Existing checkout with a free/complimentary offering and a separate paid offering.
checks.check: Complete the free flow. Separately decline a sandbox payment, correct the payment method and retry. Confirm the rejected attempt creates no extra charge or issued admission and the final sale exists once. For an uncertain result, inspect the original order before retrying.
checks.why: Free/payment-mode handling and purchase tracking changed.
checks.clients: Public Web and Widget; staff recovery only where the client provides it

checks.title: Preserve money through Refund, Void and Exchange
checks.start: Separate prepared paid orders, including a package and a voucher-funded purchase.
checks.check: Run Refund, Void and Exchange as separate journeys. Compare expected returned/retained money, credits, fees/taxes and Showpass earnings with fresh records. Check selected items, untouched items, final validity and released Inventory. A correct Customer total alone is insufficient.
checks.why: Voucher restoration, package credit and fee allocation changed.
checks.clients: Supported Customer and staff adjustment paths; use the actual payment/credit policy

checks.title: Keep existing package and hold quantities correct
checks.start: An existing package with included tickets from child Events, a standalone ticket and prepared held Inventory.
checks.check: Buy the package plus the standalone ticket and compare Review with the issued quantities. Release or expire a separate hold through its supported path and prove the released places can be purchased. Include a controlled competing last-place check through existing coverage.
checks.why: Shared reservation and parent/child counting changed.
checks.clients: Public Web, Widget and affected staff sales; new pool rule matrices stay with the feature team

checks.title: Keep memberships, admission and transfers working
checks.start: A prepared active Member, an inactive Member and a transferable game ticket.
checks.check: Verify an ordinary membership purchase retains its promised benefits. An active Member can redeem an eligible benefit; an inactive Member is denied and another benefit stays unchanged. Transfer the selected game once; confirm the recipient’s access and the sender’s resulting ticket state.
checks.why: Membership access lookup and transfer navigation changed.
checks.clients: Web Check In and the supported mobile scanner; My Orders for the transfer

checks.title: Preserve saved Event settings and local times
checks.start: Dashboard → Manage Events → Edit an existing Event with saved ticket and fee settings.
checks.check: Change one permitted setting, save and reopen it; confirm sibling Ticket Types and unrelated settings remain unchanged. Compare one known Event time through public listing, checkout, My Orders and delivery. Preserve an older paid order when checking the edited catalog.
checks.why: Draft initialization, schedule adapters and financial editing changed.
checks.clients: Dashboard plus the corresponding Customer views; teams test new scheduling options

checks.title: Keep established public entry paths available
checks.start: An existing Organizer profile, Event link and embedded Widget on desktop and phone width.
checks.check: Reach the same offering through visible navigation, retain selection through checkout/login, and complete the existing journey. Check legacy guest-list embeds when rollout is off; use the team-accepted enabled setup for coexistence checks. Recheck configured Queue-it entry without changing its configuration.
checks.why: Public profiles, shared search, embeds and navigation changed.
checks.clients: Desktop/phone Public Web and existing Widgets; the new guest-list acceptance matrix belongs to its team

checks.title: Keep existing approvals and access restrictions intact
checks.start: An existing publication workflow and ordinary employee accounts with allowed, denied and other-Organization access.
checks.check: Submit and review an ordinary request through its notification link. Confirm the current submission and PDF answers match. Check that an ordinary login still works and denied employees or another Organization cannot read or change the protected records.
checks.why: Workflow lifecycle and the shared authentication chain changed.
checks.clients: Dashboard and existing session/API clients; new key-scope and pricing-preview acceptance stays with the teams

checks.title: Reconcile receipt, reports and tracking for known orders
checks.start: The orders preserved from the checks above, plus a prepared gift card.
checks.check: Open delivered order/ticket links and the gift-card redemption link on the intended host. Match Transactions/export quantities and amounts to those known orders and adjustments. Confirm the purchase is not counted again after receipt reload; check the authorized analytics destination when available.
checks.why: Email links, revenue allocation and tracking changed.
checks.clients: Actual controlled inbox/output, Transactions/export and authorized analytics reads

regression_plan.setup: Before execution, use the release build, team-confirmed Venue flags/settings, prepared disposable records, approved sandbox payments and supported cleanup. Start with the First checks. Reuse existing saved cases/automation where their assertions prove the stated result; no Qase or automation coverage audit was performed.
regression_plan.clients: Client scope: Public Web, existing Widgets and Web Box Office. The desktop app starts the same Box Office page, and mobile/POS reuses the shared basket service, so include staff-sale smoke on supported Electron and mobile/POS builds. Exercise physical terminals, printing and mobile scanning on the actual configured devices; browser results cannot replace device proof. Use only controls the client supports.
regression_plan.result_rules: Record results for each check and client as Passed, Failed, Blocked or Not run, with the tested build and evidence. Missing setup, device access or final money/Inventory/admission proof is Blocked, not a pass. Keep initial failures and incomplete background results visible. Do not clear money, fee-revenue or access failures because feature-team acceptance passed.
